checks: At non-knot s both index groups are nonempty. Equal signed-height contributions recover α,β from the section and the barycentric sum recovers the common factor 1/L. Boundary group coordinates are handled by the closed formula and have no extra volume.

In the orthant, x_i=Sλ_i gives S^m, and D=S(height-s) has derivative S in the height variable. At S=1 these factors are one. The physical ambient determinant m!V and first-coordinate coarea one recover the physical slice measure.

Rescaling by δ_i gives its inverse product determinant. Radial powers u^(|I|-1)v^(|J|-1), the 1/L radial determinant, and u=v=1/L give L^(-m) exactly. A direct d=2 balanced-group simplex gives a square of area 1/4 and a diagonal cap of area 1/8, agreeing with the formula.

At a nonvertical cap its limiting equality hyperplane is d-null, so slice limits give the actual cut volumes. Pure-base caps instead use the exact closed indicator at each height. Source §5 and exact replay agree.

overlap.comparison: The ordinary scalar tail is a whole simplex halfspace volume, not an arbitrary second cap restricted to a fixed section with a common ambient normal.
Its explicit sampled cap is a canonical vertex homothet. The product integral handles arbitrary affine vertex values for the common cut.

readability: The auxiliary D and S refer to orthant variables; evaluating their disintegration at (1,0) keeps the physical first-coordinate Jacobian clear.

summary: The projective product formula retains the actual cap, uses the correct disintegration determinant, and handles knot and vertical cases.
